question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{({n}^{3}-2)({n}^{3}+2)}{({n}^{2}-3)({n}^{2}+3)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{({n}^{3}-2)({n}^{3}+2)}{({n}^{2}-3)({n}^{2}+3)}=\frac{{n}^{6}-4}{{n}^{4}-9}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{n}^{6}-4}{{n}^{4}-9}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is ${n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{n}^{6}-4}{{n}^{4}-9} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{n}^{6}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{4}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{({n}^{2}-\frac{4}{{n}^{4}})}{(1-\frac{9}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{n}^{2}-0}{1-0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{n}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence diverges.
